content:
elaine-cs: quick heads-up — ThinClient onboarding hit a tail-latency bump in prod this morning. saw p95 ~720ms on generation route for long prompts. renewal call in 6w. want to propose a low-risk perf plan to present to customer + ops handoff :clipboard:
marcus-ml: ok. can you paste example trace or request shape? initial thought: compact model swap + int8 quantization for non-critical endpoints. should save 30-40% cost and cut p95 ~200ms for that workload depending on seq len
katie-se: customer uses heavy context + embeddings lookup before gen. they do a lot of short follow-ups too. swapping the primary model could change output style — need to capture a few prompt-templates for QA. also they rely on function-calls in ~12% of requests
elaine-cs: attaching a short sample from logs (redacted):
```
user_id=acme-thin prompt_tokens=512 history_tokens=1024 model=redwood-l/longform-v1 seq=1536
latencies: routing=30ms kvcache=90ms decode=600ms
```
marcus-ml: perfect. given seq distribution, quick wins: 1) enable prefix KV caching for repeated history token sets 2) route follow-ups to a compact-finetuned variant (redwood-c/fewshot-compact) for short seqs 3) int8 quant for the larger model + fallback to fp16 if regen quality drops
jordan-eng: from infra side we can do a canary rollout. propose: 5% traffic -> compact model for 48h, monitor perplexity/ROUGE proxy + p95 latency + error rate. canary config snippet for routing policy:
```
route: gen
  policy:
    - predicate: request.tokens_total <= 600
      model: redwood-c/fewshot-compact
      weight: 0.05
    - predicate: default
      model: redwood-l/longform-v1-int8
      weight: 0.95
```
opsbot: dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/thinclient/perf (live p95, token-cost, quality-proxy) :link:
sam-csm: i'll loop in ThinClient PM and schedule a 30m sync after we collect 24h canary data. also capturing risk note for renewal: "if we can't improve p95 by 150-200ms, expect negotiation on price" — want this included in renewal prep doc
katie-se: for QA, i'll assemble 12 representative prompt-templates and an eval harness. we should measure token-level divergence and a small humanscore sample on 50 pairs pre/post-swap. also flag function-call fidelity: ensure compact variant respects schema and tool calling at parity
marcus-ml: technical caveats: int8 quant on the long model reduces memory by ~2.8x but may increase decode variance on rare tokens. plan: enable per-layer quant calibration and a short regen check (1000 samples). fallback rule: if quality-proxy delta > 0.06, revert to fp16 for affected shards
jordan-eng: provisioning note: will spin a dedicated canary pool in eu-west-1 to match customer's region. need approval for ~2x inference capacity for 72h to absorb canary and baseline traffic — ops bill estimate ~ $1.8k. pinging infra budget channel separately
elaine-cs: approved to proceed with canary and QA. next steps: marcus -> run calibration + synthetic regen check (ETA 24h), katie -> eval harness + prompt set (ETA 24h), jordan -> canary pool + routing rule (ETA 18h), sam -> schedule customer sync after 24h of canary data. i'll draft renewal note and circulate
sam-csm: noted. i'll capture customer concerns in the sync agenda: latency targets, output tone, function-call fidelity, and escalation path. want to propose "30-day rollback window" in contract addendum if we swap models
marcus-ml: starting calibration now. will post a short artifact with calibration metrics and top-10 failure cases.
elaine-cs: thanks team. small ask: if we hit quality regressions, prioritize a hybrid route: keep critical routes on fp16 longform and route non-critical short follow-ups to compact variant. i'll include that in the customer-facing one-pager. :white_check_mark:
